question: What problem does adjusted R squared fix compared with plain R squared?
answer: adjusted R squared fixes the issue that plain R squared can increase when adding predictors, unlike adjusted R squared which does not decrease when a predictor is added to the model, ensuring a fair comparison of models of different sizes [S1] [S3] [S4] [S5].

It does not mean "typical" or "healthy" values.  standardization: in this course standardization means converting values to z-scores with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. adjusted R squared: adjusted R2 = 1 - (1 - R2) * (n - 1) / (n - p - 1) where p is the number of predictors. Plain R2 never decreases when a predictor is added to the model, so adjusted R2 is used to compare models of different sizes. sample: in statistics a sample is a subset drawn from a population. citations.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
citations.text: 6. Correlation and Regression Correlation measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables. The Pearson correlation coefficient r ranges from -1 to +1. A value near +1 indicates a strong positive linear relationship, near -1 a strong negative one and near 0 no linear relationship. Correlation does not imply causation: a hidden confounding variable may drive both variables. Simple linear regression fits the line y-hat = b0 + b1 * x by least squares, which minimizes the sum of squared residuals. The slope b1 equals r * (s_y / s_x) and the intercept is b0 = y-bar - b1 * x-bar. The coefficient of determination R squared is the proportion of variance in y explained by the model; in simple regression it equals r squared. Residual plots should show no pattern; curved or funnel-shaped residuals indicate a violated assumption.

S2.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S2.text:
5. Regression Metrics and Calibration
RMSE is expressed in the same units as the target, which makes it easy to interpret. R squared
can be negative on test data: that happens when the model predicts worse than simply predicting
the mean of the target.
Probability calibration asks whether predicted probabilities match observed frequencies. A
reliability diagram is the usual plot for inspecting calibration.
